samples.summary: The claim population is narrower than the population adjudicate.mjs labelled: validity excludes items whose envelope status is not `ok`, but adjudicate queues findings from every stored item, so labels for a failed-but-productive replay join as `unmatched`
samples.evidence: `validity.mjs:1116` skips any item where `item.envelope?.status !== "ok"` when building the panel claim population. The producer of the labels does no such filtering: `adjudicate.mjs:1021-1022` does `for (const runId of opts.runs) for (const item of runRecords(store, runId, { population: "reported", itemId: opts.itemId })) records.push(...item.records)` — and a grep for `envelope`/`status` anywhere in `adjudicate.mjs` returns nothing. `adapters/panel.mjs:247-253` (`runRecords` → `panelRecords`) likewise ignores envelope status; `panelRecords` refuses only on a missing envelope object or item_id. `run.mjs:1136-1141` stores non-`ok` items whose payload still came from a real capture (an `outcome.fatal`/non-ok status is written alongside the same `payload` built from `cap`), so findings — and therefore labels — can exist for items validity drops. Every such label then falls into `joinLabels`'s `unmatched` bucket, leaves the precision denominator, and forces `completeness.verdict = "partial"` and exit 1. It is at least reported rather than silent, but the denominator is still cut by a rule the label-writing path never applied. Fix belongs on one side or the other: either adjudicate should refuse non-`ok` items, or validity should include them and name them, rather than the two disagreeing.

samples.summary: `distinct_keys_by_stated_severity` reads `record.severity`, which is a normalised/floored value, not the reviewer's stated word — the payload and the report label it "the reviewer's own word", and a `not-measurable` justification is built on it
samples.evidence: `validity.mjs:378` buckets claims by `r.severity`, and `validity.mjs:999` prints them as `claims by STATED severity (the reviewer's own word)`; `validity.mjs:853-860` uses the same map to emit `"the arm raised no finding it called <severity> either"` as the reason a stratum is permanently not-measurable. But `finding-record.mjs:272-287` documents that `severity` is `normalizeSeverity(finding.severity)` (unknown → `major`) and states explicitly that for CodeRabbit `severity` and `severity_raw` are always equal because the adapter translated the word first — the reviewer's actual word lives at `record.coderabbit.stated_severity`. `adapters/coderabbit.mjs:354` returns `severity: UNSTATED_SEVERITY` with `severity_basis: "unstated"` when CodeRabbit stated nothing, and the repo already has the correct predicate for this: `severityIsStated` (exported from volume-mix.mjs, used at `segmentation.mjs:513` to route unstated findings into a separate `severity-unstated` bucket). validity imports neither, so floored/unstated severities are counted as though the arm had stated them, and the sentence 'the arm raised no finding it called X' can be false.

samples.summary: `--arm panel|coderabbit` filters the claim populations but not the labels read from disk, so any single-arm invocation reports the other arm as `claims-not-supplied`, is always PARTIAL, and always exits 1
samples.evidence: `validity.mjs:1096` calls `readFindingLabels(args.root, args["corpus-version"])`, which enumerates every arm directory under `labels/<cv>/findings/<item>/<arm>/` (`adjudicate.mjs:560-566`) and returns labels for both arms. Only the claim populations are gated by `--arm` (`validity.mjs:1101,1128`). `scoreValidity` then builds an arm row for every arm that has a label (`armIds` union), the un-supplied arm gets `claim_population: "unknown"` and a `no claim population supplied` reason, and `completeness.verdict` becomes `partial` → `process.exitCode = 1` (`validity.mjs:1159`). So on a store that has labels for both arms, `--arm coderabbit` can never exit 0, which defeats the flag's purpose and makes the exit code uninformative in a pipeline.

samples.summary: `validity-v1` is not registered in `report.mjs`'s SECTIONS/SCORER_IDS or `score-all.mjs`'s STEPS, so the SCORER_ID/SCOPE the payload declares can never actually be filed by the only persist path
samples.evidence: The new module exports `SCORER_ID = "validity-v1"` / `SCOPE = "cross-run"` (validity.mjs:102-103) and argues store.mjs's `validateScore` accepts it — true (store.mjs:383-404 only checks agreement, and `_scorePath` at store.mjs:995 only requires a path segment). But the only path that writes a score is `report.mjs --persist --scorer-id …`, invoked by `score-all.mjs:499`, and `report.mjs:1538-1539` refuses any id not in `SCORER_IDS`, which is derived from `SECTIONS` (report.mjs:110-119) — five ids, none of them `validity-v1`. `score-all.mjs:86-91` likewise has no validity step. The module's header says it deliberately 'adds no report section', so this may be intentional staging; recording it because the declared scorer_id/scope currently have no reachable consumer.
searchedFor: read score-all.mjs STEPS (86-91) and filing args (499)

samples.summary: `relativeRecallBand` pairing assumes `ARMS` has exactly two members; a third arm would silently give each arm an arbitrary 'other arm' rather than refusing
samples.evidence: `validity.mjs:888` picks the counterpart with `const otherArm = ARMS.find((a) => a !== armId)`. `ARMS` is owned by `finding-record.mjs:50` (`["panel", "coderabbit"]`) and is a frozen vocabulary other modules widen from (labels.mjs:553 validates `arm` against it, and adjudicate.mjs:566 deliberately enumerates arm directories 'so a tree written by a future arm is read rather than skipped'). If a third arm is ever added there, the union bounds in this band become a two-arm union computed against whichever arm `find` returns first, with no error — the same silent-wrong-denominator class the file is written to prevent. A `pin`-style import-time assertion that `ARMS.length === 2`, or an explicit refusal, would make the dependency load-bearing.

samples.summary: With two or more `--item` filters the CodeRabbit adapter is asked for the whole corpus, so every corpus item is fetched from the GitHub API and then discarded
samples.evidence: `validity.mjs:1131` passes `{ itemId: itemFilter.length === 1 ? itemFilter[0] : null }`, and `adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1136-1143` filters by `itemId` BEFORE calling `fetchCodeRabbitPr` per item — so a null itemId means a network round trip for every item in the manifest, with the filter applied afterwards at validity.mjs:1132. Correct, but it makes `--item a --item b` markedly more expensive than `--item a`, contrary to the USAGE's cost note.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. validity.mjs:1116-1119 excludes any item whose `envelope.status !== "ok"` from the panel claim population, while the label producer applies no such rule: adjudicate.mjs:1021-1022 queues records for every stored item, and grep for `envelope`/`status` in adjudicate.mjs returns no matches. The intermediate readers ignore status too — adapters/panel.mjs:247-253 (`runRecords`) and :218-242 (`panelRecords`) refuse only on a missing envelope object or empty item_id, and store.mjs:917-948 does no filtering. The path is reachable: run.mjs:1097-1141 stores `payload` built from the real capture alongside non-`ok` statuses, and classifyItemOutcome (run.mjs:245-299) returns `gate-degraded` / `no-lens-diff` / `infra` / `no-output` for items whose panel exited 0 with a present panel.json, for which adapters/reviewer.mjs:440-490 populates `payload.findings` and adapters/panel.mjs:133-144 turns them into records. Labels written for such items then hit joinLabels (validity.mjs:419-427) as `unmatched`, drop out of the precision denominator (validity.mjs:787-788, 830-833), add a reason (validity.mjs:817-818) and force `completeness.verdict = "partial"` with exit 1 (validity.mjs:934-935, 1160). This is a cross-module population/invariant disagreement between the label producer and the new scorer consuming those labels — in-lane and blocking at major; no guard or caller makes it unreachable.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. validity.mjs:378-379 buckets claim keys by `r.severity` into `distinct_keys_by_stated_severity` (line 396), the docblock at line 363 calls it "THE REVIEWER's severity", line 999 prints it as "claims by STATED severity (the reviewer's own word)", and lines 853/869 use `stated === 0` to emit "the arm raised no finding it called <severity> either" as the reason a stratum is permanently not-measurable. But `record.severity` is not the stated word: finding-record.mjs:272 sets it via `normalizeSeverity`, and its own comment at 276-287 states that for CodeRabbit `severity`/`severity_raw` are always the translated value and the reviewer's word lives at `coderabbit.stated_severity`. adapters/coderabbit.mjs:354 returns `severity: UNSTATED_SEVERITY` ("nit", line 303) with `severity_basis: "unstated"` when CodeRabbit stated nothing, documented at 290-301 as a deliberate floor; line 353 derives severity from a tier heading rather than a stated word. The repo already has the right predicate for this distinction — segmentation.mjs:510-514 uses `severityIsStated` (imported at segmentation.mjs:63) to keep unstated apart from "the floor value it would otherwise inherit" — and validity.mjs imports neither `severityIsStated` nor reads `severity_basis` anywhere (imports at validity.mjs:68-77). It is reachable: validity.mjs:1128-1139 feeds CodeRabbit adapter records straight into the arm legs consumed by claimCensus at line 774. So floored/unstated severities are counted and reported as words the arm "called" its findings, and the not-measurable justification is built on that map. Contract-vs-consumer mismatch on an exported record field, real and reachable; nothing guards it and I found no ground to call it out of lane.
